task: Should the box fall, make your very next move the one that picks it back up. If you get to the exit, you must have the box in your hands.

calls.candidate: hard Existence(at_exit), hard Precedence(holding_box, at_exit), hard Response(box_fell, holding_box)
calls.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: two mismatches. (1) The task says the very next move after a fall must pick the box back up, i.e. holding_box on the very next step, but the clause Response(box_fell, holding_box) only requires holding_box at some later step, dropping the timing. Replace it with hard ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box). (2) The task's second sentence is 'If you get to the exit, you must have the box in your hands', which is 'if a happens, c must hold', so the right template is hard Response(at_exit, holding_box) (at_exit is a last-step condition, so holding_box must hold on that step). The clause Precedence(holding_box, at_exit) is the wrong template: since holding_box is true from the first step, it is satisfied immediately and does not require the box at the exit. Keep the hard Existence(at_exit) (the environment's objective is to reach the exit) and add Response(at_exit, holding_box) in place of the Precedence.

calls.candidate: hard ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box), hard Existence(at_exit), hard Response(at_exit, holding_box)
calls.feedback: NO CHANGES NEEDED: Existence(at_exit) is the task's stated objective (reach the exit); Response(at_exit, holding_box) makes the box-in-hands requirement hold on the exit step; ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box) requires the very next step after each fall to have the box picked back up, matching 'your very next move'.
